issues.description: Field SealSaloon.orders: The problem statement (UML and textual description) requires a modifiable List<Meal> named `orders`. The provided starter/utility code (ArrayHelpers) and the reference solution declare and use an array type `Meal[]` for orders (see SealSaloon.java: `private Meal[] orders;`). This mismatch between the specified type (List<Meal>) and the actual concrete type used in the template/solution (Meal[]) creates ambiguity for students about which type to implement and whether they should use java.util.List or the provided ArrayHelpers/arrays.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and starter code consistent. Option A: Update the problem statement and UML to require an array-based `orders` (Meal[]) and explicitly mention students should use the provided ArrayHelpers to modify the orders array. Option B: Change the template/solution to use `java.util.List<Meal>` (initialize orders as e.g. new ArrayList<>()) and update all code and the UML accordingly. Ensure the textual description, UML, and starter files all reference the same concrete type.

issues.description: Constructor initialization guidance in the problem statement: The problem text instructs that SealSaloon should initialize attributes to default values but gives a combined example "e.g., an empty list or a new object of the class Stock" in a way that mixes which default applies to which attribute. The reference solution initializes `orders` as an empty array in the constructor and declares `stock` as a static final Stock initialized at its declaration. The ambiguous wording may lead students to misunderstand whether `orders` should be an empty collection/array and whether `stock` should be initialized in the constructor or elsewhere.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the constructor initialization guidance in the problem statement. Explicitly state: "Initialize `orders` to an empty list (or an empty array if arrays are used) in the constructor, and initialize `stock` to a new Stock() instance (or declare it as a static final initialized at declaration if the design requires it)." Make this guidance consistent with the chosen data structure for orders (List vs array) and with whether `stock` is static/final.
